script:
Good morning, and welcome to Market Digest for Wednesday, November 11th. Here's what mattered today, in about three minutes.

First, the AI trade came back to life. CoreWeave, a company that rents out computing power for artificial intelligence, beat expectations and raised its outlook. Its shares jumped about 26 percent, and the Nasdaq 100 rose about 3 percent. Investors took it as a sign that spending on AI is still paying off, though some analysts pointed out that CoreWeave is funding its growth with debt and customer prepayments, and that carries risk.

Second, the scandal around Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, keeps growing. He faces allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia's stock is down more than 30 percent since the story broke, Congress wants him to testify, and the company has hired an outside law firm to investigate. It's a textbook case of key-person risk: when a company's value is closely tied to one leader, doubts about that person can hit the stock hard.

Third, inflation. Consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in October, hotter than economists expected. The two-year Treasury yield, which tracks what markets expect the Federal Reserve to do, jumped to 4.78 percent, and prediction markets put the odds of a December rate hike at about 86 percent. Why would the Fed raise rates? Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which cools spending and slows price rises.

In AI companies, the WSJ reported that OpenAI's quarterly revenue reached about 10 billion dollars, but it's still losing a lot of money, while Anthropic brought in 17 billion with much smaller losses. Remember: revenue is money coming in, profit is what's left after costs. Anthropic's stock market debut is drawing heavy demand.

It was also a rough stretch for some big names. Alphabet had its worst day ever, down about 12.6 percent, Intel fell almost 29 percent after disappointing results, and the crypto exchange Binance lost 6.3 billion dollars to hackers.

Today's concept is market concentration. The 10 biggest companies now make up about 40 percent of the S&P 500's value, compared with 16 percent ten years ago. So if you own an S&P 500 index fund, a big move in a few giants like Nvidia moves your fund a lot more than it used to.

Coming up: the December Fed meeting, Anthropic's IPO, and Jensen Huang's appearance before Congress.

That's your digest. Try today's three-question quiz in the app, and remember, nothing here is financial advice. See you tomorrow.
